title: Substream merge and tail-squelch: tenant flow shaping + kernel hinting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Some multi-tenant workloads show pathological P95/P99 spikes during mixed short/long-request bursts. Current admission heuristics admit tokens at a tenant granularity which over-fragments kernel seating and prevents efficient attention prefetching, increasing decode tail latency for small interactive requests.

Goal: Implement a flow-oriented 'substream merge' layer that: 1) groups short concurrent requests from the same tenant into transient substreams for admission and kernel fitting, 2) applies a tail-squelch policy to delay non-critical prefill work when it would unacceptably increase short-request latency, and 3) emit kernel-hint metadata so the scheduler can pick the best kernel path (int8/quantized tiles vs fused attention) per merged substream.

Approach:
- Admission: instead of fixed per-request admission windows, allow ephemeral substreams that can accept additional short requests for up to 6ms or until a token-size threshold (configurable). Substream time/window parameters will be tenant-configurable and default to conservative values for high-SLO tenants.
- Batch shaping: within a substream, compute a mixed-batch shape that prioritizes preserving low-latency slots. Use a fast heuristic to decide if an incoming short request fits a hot micro-batch (fast path) or should be staged to a separate prefill wave (background path).
- Kernel hinting: derive light-weight hints (attention-friendly, kv-cache-likely, prefer-quant) from token-length distribution and recent kernel latency/throughput stats; attach hints to admission tokens so the kernel scheduler can prefer matching kernels without an expensive probe.
- Tail-squelch: implement a defeasible delay for background prefill (e.g., embeddings-heavy or long-prefill) when the scheduler is near latency targets; these delayed prefill items will be retried with exponential backoff and will not block critical short-path requests.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Increased admission complexity and more state per GPU (substream metadata). Mitigation: keep substream state compact and TTL the state aggressively.
- Risk of added jitter for non-interactive long jobs. Mitigation: configurable tenant policies; background path ensures progress with bounded backoff.
- Kernel-hint inaccuracies could cause suboptimal kernel selection. Mitigation: record feedback and incorporate online correction rules in later cycles.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/CBv3-substream-merge (internal)
- Kernel hinting RFC: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/kernel-hints-rfc
- Benchmark dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/g/batching/ENG-47218
- Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/9482

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end P99 latency for short-interactive benchmark reduces by >=15% at 95th percentile load on mixed short/long workload scenario (internal bench harness).
- No more than 5% throughput regression on long-prefill-heavy synthetic workloads vs baseline when tenant uses default settings.
- Kernel scheduler accepts hint metadata and chooses a different kernel at least 70% of the time when hint indicates a clear preference (validated by test harness).
- Feature gated behind runtime flag and per-tenant config with safe defaults; rollout plan exists.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests: admission window edge cases, substream TTL expiry, hint attach/detach behavior.
- Integration tests: simulated mixed-workload on local cluster with deterministic traffic generator; validate metrics and request traces.
- Chaos/soak: 24h soak on dedicated internal cluster with adversarial burst patterns.

Monitoring and rollbacks:
- New metrics: substream_created, substream_join_rate, substream_steal_count, tail_squelch_delay_ms, kernel_hint_match_rate.
- Dashboards and alerts: P99 short-path latency increase >10% triggers automatic rollback to previous runtime flag.

Rollout plan:
- Canary: enable for 5% of traffic on low-SLA tenants for 48h.
- Ramp: 25% -> 75% -> 100% over two weeks with metric gates.

Long-term: If successful, fold substream logic into the tenant-aware admission service and enrich hints with learned policies from Optimize (model recommendations).

2026-03-10 — Metrics after small internal canary (48h): P99 short-path went down 16% on canary nodes; tail_squelch_delay_ms median 2.3ms, 99th 18ms. No user-facing errors. Proceeding to wider ramp pending QA soak. — Marco
notes: Implementation should minimize per-GPU memory: store substream header as 64-bit compact state + small TTL bucket.
Keep hint encoding extensible and low-overhead; prefer enums (1 byte) and a uint16 score for confidence.
Work with Optimize team to collect post-rollout quality regressions and map hint triggers to model/eval sets.
